Blocks.Name: BarChart
Blocks.Description:
The bar chart is a two-dimensional chart where rectangular bars are placed along the x axis with bar length representing the value for a specific category.
To customize the elements of the chart (X axis, Y axis, Series Legend, Series, or Tooltip) drag-and-drop the addons into the ChartAddons placeholder inside the Chart block. 
Note: the addons SS preview won't be visible in runtime.

Inputs.Name: DataPointList
Inputs.Description:
Data that will be used in the chart.Create an aggregate with your data and use it in this field to populate the chart.

Structure:
- Value (Decimal) Mandatory - The value to be plotted.
- Label (Text) Mandatory - The label of the data point.
- SeriesName (Text) - The name of the series where the data point belongs.
- Color (Text) - The color of the data point. By default, the chart will be presented with the OutSystems data visualization color palette. To define a custom color for a series, use the Color property of the ChartSeriesStyling block.
- Tooltip (Text) - The text that will be displayed on the tooltip of the data point.By default, the tooltip contains the label and value of the point, following the structure [Label]: [Value]. Example: "Apples: 58"

Inputs.Name: Height
Inputs.Description: Set the vertical size, in px or %, of the chart. By default, the vertical size is 300px.

Inputs.Name: StackingType
ValuesType
Inputs.Description:
Set how the chart labels are handled to be displayed on the chart.
The type of the values can be:
 - Integer: the labels will be displayed as integer numbers.
 - Decimal: the labels will be displayed as decimal numbers.
 - Datetime: the labels will be displayed as datetimes.
 - Text: the labels will be displayed as text and treated as categories.
By default, the type is Text.

Inputs.Name: OptionalConfigs
Inputs.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the bar chart behavior and functionality.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

Events.Name: Initialized
Events.Description: Event triggered after the chart instance is ready.

Events.Description: Event triggered when the chart’s data is clicked. It returns information about the chart and data point that was clicked.

Params.Name: DataPoint
Params.Description: Details about the chart point that was clicked: label, value, name of the series, tooltip content, and color.

- Value (Decimal) Mandatory - The value to be plotted.
- Label (Text) Mandatory - The label of the data point.
- SeriesName (Text) - The name of the series where the data point belongs.
- Color (Text) - The color of the data point. By default, the chart will be presented with the OutSystems data visualization color palette. To define a custom color for a series, use the Color property of the ChartSeriesStyling block.
- Tooltip (Text) - The text that will be displayed on the tooltip of the data point. By default, the tooltip contains the label and value of the point, following the structure [Label]: [Value]. Example: "Apples: 58"

 -Bottom

- Horizontal
- Vertical

Events.Name: Loaded
Events.Description: Event triggered when the High Charts modules are successfully loaded into the application. It is important to note that if a module that has already been loaded is not added again, and will not have any effect and but will trigger this event.

Params.Name: AddedNewModules
Params.Description: When set to true, it indicates that at least one module that was not previously present on the page has been added during the loading process. This parameter serves as an indicator to highlight the addition of new modules.

Events.Name: LoadError
Events.Description:
Event triggered when the an error(s) occurs during the loading of HighCharts modules into the OutSystems application. T
his event provides essential information about the encountered error(s), enabling developers to take appropriate actions to handle these errors gracefully. 
It's important to note that if multiple modules are being loaded and one of them fails, the LoadError event will be triggered. However, the remaining modules were successfully loaded and the changes are reflected in the charts.

Params.Name: MessageList
Params.Description: Each string within the array represents an error message associated with a specific module that failed to load. These messages provide details about the specific issues that occurred, such as the non-existence of a module.

Structures.Name: ChartLegendOptionalConfigs
Structures.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the chart series legend behavior and functionality.

Attributes.Name: Floating
Attributes.Description: Set to True to the legend above the chart. By default, False.

Attributes.Name: Visible
Attributes.Description: Set to True to display the X axis and its elements on the chart. False, otherwise. By default, the Y axis is visible.

Attributes.Name: Position
Attributes.Description:
Set the Legend's position (Default: Bottom). The predefined options are:
    -Bottom
    -BottomLeft
    -BottomRight
    -Center
    -Left
    -Right
    -Top
    -TopLeft
    -TopRight

Examples:
    Entities.Position.Right - The Legend is displayed to the right of the chart.Entities.
    Position.Bottom - The Legend is displayed underneath the chart.

Attributes.Name: Layout
Attributes.Description:
The layout of the legend items. The layout of the legend can be: 
    - Horizontal
    - Vertical
    - Proximate: the legend items will be placed as close as possible to the graphs they're representing, except in inverted charts or when the legend position doesn't allow it.

By default, the legend layout is horizontal.

Attributes.Name: ExtendedClass
Attributes.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.
Examples:
    - Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
    - "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
    - "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

Attributes.Name: BackgroundColor
Attributes.Description: Set the background color of the legend. By default, the legend has no background color (transparent).

Attributes.Name: ItemsDistance
Attributes.Description: Set the distance between the items, in pixels, of the legend. By default, the items have a distance of 20px between them.

Attributes.Name: Floating
Attributes.Description: Set to True to have place the legend above the chart. By default, False.
